breaks.expected: After an owner generation change the previous chain is gone in every observable way (tryAgainStackDepth() === 0, peekTryAgainOrigin() === null), whether or not its top hop had been consumed.
breaks.observed: Owner A: arm→consume, arm→consume (depth 2). Switch to owner B: peekTryAgainOrigin() is null and consume returns null, but tryAgainStackDepth() stays 2 (A→B→A variant: 1) and nothing is recorded. The candidate's own test pins depth 0 + 'owner_changed' for the same switch when the top hop is still pending, so the module's post-switch state depends on whether the last hop was consumed. breaks.title: Dead chain lingers after an owner change when the top hop was already consumed (depth reports the previous owner's hops; no owner_changed telemetry)

breaks.expected: The 'original clip retry entry' the module claims to preserve cannot be altered through references handed out to callers (freeze or copy on arm/consume).
breaks.observed: armTryAgain stores the caller's object by reference and consume/peekTryAgainOrigin return that same reference (not frozen, not copied). Writing declaredStroke/sessionId on the consumed object changes peekTryAgainOrigin(); writing auto/declaredStroke on the armed object after the tap changes what consume returns. VERIFIED fails 2/2 on candidate; the arm-side aliasing also fails on BASE (pre-existing). INFERRED: current shipping callers (ResultScreen/ResultDetailsScreen/FormReviewScreen pass a fresh tryAgainFromResult object; AnalyzeScreen only reads `rearm`) do not mutate, so no user-visible effect today.
breaks.title: Hops alias caller objects: mutating the handoff returned by consume rewrites the preserved 'original clip' origin; mutating the object passed to armTryAgain rewrites the pending hop

breaks.expected: The origin is the retry armed from the clip the current loop started from; a TRY AGAIN from a Result belonging to a different practice set / clip starts a new chain (or the objective defines chain boundaries explicitly).
breaks.observed: Owner A: Try Again from clip in set-1 (arm→consume), then Try Again from a different clip in set-2 (arm→consume). peekTryAgainOrigin() returns the set-1 handoff. The only chain boundaries are owner-generation change, TTL expiry of a pending hop, and clearTryAgainHandoff (saved-analysis route mount / non-camera Analyze mount); tapping TRY AGAIN on a different clip's Result is treated as hop N of the old chain. VERIFIED fails 1/1 on candidate. Note the candidate's own test uses distinct sessionIds per hop and expects one chain, so this is a semantics disagreement with the objective's 'original clip retry entry'; nothing in the shipping app reads peekTryAgainOrigin, so no user-visible effect.
breaks.title: Chain identity is not tied to the clip/practice set: a Try Again from a different saved clip continues the previous chain, so the 'original clip' origin is the wrong clip

implement.summary: Defect on BASE (apps/mobile/src/screens/tryAgainHandoff.ts:50-90): the Try Again handoff was a single mutable slot (pendingHandoff/pendingArmedAtMs) bounded only by a 30s TTL. It carried no DataOwnerContext, so a handoff armed under account A was consumed after switching to B or after A->B->A (new generation) — consumeTryAgainHandoff returned the stale handoff (VERIFIED: w09TryAgainStack.test.ts fails 8/12 on BASE, artifacts/w09-08/ac1-base.log) — and repeated Result -> TRY AGAIN -> Analyze cycles kept no bounded chain or original-clip retry entry. Fix (only inside write_paths): the module now keeps `hops: TryAgainHop[]` bounded by TRY_AGAIN_STACK_LIMIT=3 — the bottom hop is the retry armed from the original clip and is preserved while older intermediate hops are evicted; each hop records getDataOwnerSnapshot() (ownerKey+generation from src/data/accountScope.ts) at arm time; consume/peek reject a hop whose ownerKey or generation differs, recording stabilitySlo try_again_failed reason 'owner_changed' and dropping the chain; TTL expiry still records 'handoff_expired'; re-arming over an unconsumed hop replaces it (existing single-shot semantics preserved); clearTryAgainHandoff drops the whole chain; arming under a new owner generation starts a fresh chain instead of reviving old state. New exports peekTryAgainOrigin/tryAgainStackDepth pin the chain. Wiring: shipping callers are unchanged and exercise the new behaviour — ResultScreen/ResultDetailsScreen/FormReviewScreen call armTryAgain then navigate('Analyze',{source:'camera'}); AnalyzeScreen calls consumeTryAgainHandoff; RootNavigator/AnalyzeScreen call clearTryAgainHandoff. VERIFIED: AC1 (12/12), AC2 (exit 0), AC3 (exit 0), pnpm format:check (exit 0), git diff --check (exit 0); related suites 206/206 (artifacts/w09-08/related-suites.log); full apps/mobile jest 5898 passed / 1 pre-existing skipped / exit 0 (artifacts/w09-08/full-mobile-jest.log).
